text:
incident-bot: 🔔 Paging eng-oncall: cont-batch path p99 spike detected in US-WEST-2. SLOs breached for streaming routes. Details: p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 2.6s, error rate stable. Auto-page triggered.

amber_oncall: I see the alert, taking this. Confirming customer impact and mitigation plan. @sam_infra can you pull recent scheduler metrics?

sam_infra: grabbing charts now. There's a sudden increase in heterogeneous seq lengths from a few customers causing big batches to form with long KV refreshes. Scheduler fairness weight dropped for streaming lanes. Looks like packer pushed a big 256-token request mix right at 17:01 UTC.

julia_sre: Observed streaming stalls where the first tokens stream fine then stall for the tail. Traces show long queue wait (>> 1s) before execution on cont-batch. KV cache eviction spikes at the same time.

amber_oncall: Customer impact: CS says three mid-market customers reported degraded chat responsiveness. Not a full outage but UX stall. @cs-ops can you log affected customer IDs?

cs-ops: Logged 2 customers in us-west-2 (cust-4021, cust-8893). Notified them: we told them we're investigating and have an ETA ~30m.

nic_engineer: Quick triage notes: mixed-seqlen workload causes the batcher to pack long and short seqs together; long sequences dominate GPU time, short ones wait -> tail p99. Also streaming requests get starved because of packer greedy scheduling.

amber_oncall: Mitigations to try (prioritized):
1) Immediately reduce max_batch_size for streaming class from 128 -> 32 to force smaller packs (low-risk rollback).
2) Apply fairness boost to streaming queue (weight +2) so streaming preempts long-batch packing.
3) Temporarily lower KV cache TTL for this host group to reduce KV churn.
4) If still high, route streaming traffic to a smaller model variant (quantized) in the same region as fallback.

sam_infra: I can push (1) and (2) now. Pushing config change to the batcher with a short TTL (5m) so it auto-reverts unless we confirm.

amber_oncall: Do it. Post the exact commands/changes.

sam_infra: Running:
```
# reduce streaming batch size
redwoodctl batcher update --env prod --region us-west-2 --class streaming --max-batch-size 32 --ttl 300
# fairness weight bump
redwoodctl batcher update --env prod --region us-west-2 --queue streaming --fairness-weight 3 --ttl 300
```
Applied at 1718887830.

incident-bot: change accepted by config-service, rollout started.

julia_sre: After change: p95 dropped to ~210ms, p99 trending down to ~1.1s within 45s. Streaming stalls reduced in traces (less queue_wait). KV eviction still slightly elevated.

nic_engineer: Suggest also tuning packer preempt threshold so that if a long job is about to block streaming for >500ms it yields. We have a quick patch to lower preempt threshold from 2000ms -> 500ms.

amber_oncall: Is preempt patch safe to hot-reload?

sam_infra: It's a runtime flag; I'll enable it with TTL 10m. Command:
```
redwoodctl runtime-flag set --region us-west-2 --flag packer.preempt_threshold_ms=500 --ttl=600
```
Applying now (1718887865).

incident-bot: runtime-flag change applied.

julia_sre: Nice — tail traces show preemption allowed streaming tasks to schedule sooner. p99 now ~760ms. Customer reports reduce perceived stalls.

amber_oncall: Good. Action items before we close the page:
- Keep the batch size & fairness changes for another 30m, monitor.
- Run a targeted load test with mixed seq lengths to reproduce and confirm packer preempt behavior. (owner: nic_engineer)
- Prepare a follow-up config: an adaptive batch cap per-client or seqlen bucketing (owner: sam_infra + nic_engineer).
- CS to send customer postmortem note after we confirm root cause. (owner: cs-ops)

nic_engineer: I'll spin the mixed-seqlen load harness against staging scheduler and capture scheduler logs + KV metrics. Plan: try sequence distributions skewed 80/20 short/long and 50/50.

cs-ops: I'll draft customer message: short summary, mitigation steps taken, ETA for full writeup.

amber_oncall: Monitoring checklist: watch p95/p99 on streaming routes, scheduler queue depth, KV eviction rate, batcher pack composition (avg batch length distribution). If p99 climbs back >1.5s, re-open page and fallback to model routing.

sam_infra: Confirming metrics dashboard pinned and alert thresholds lowered for now. Also capturing the config diffs we applied for postmortem.

incident-bot: Page closed by amber_oncall at 1718887899. Summary: applied streaming batch size cap and fairness weight, enabled packer preempt; p99 reduced from 2.6s -> ~760ms. Follow-ups assigned.

amber_oncall: Closing notes: root cause likely scheduling fairness + heterogeneous batch packing amplified by KV churn. Proposed long-term fixes: adaptive batching by seqlen, streaming-priority fast-path (dedicated small-batch pods), and smarter KV eviction heuristics. I'll hand this to the oncall rotation notes. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
